The trend_dominated regime suggests that focusing on models that capture trend well might be beneficial, so I will test a softmax-weighted combination over the full pool to see if a more aggressive weighting of top performers improves the score.

The trend_dominated regime suggests that selecting a subset of models that capture this upward trend effectively, rather than using all models, might be beneficial. I will test a median combination of the top-performing models from the most stable pools to reduce the influence of potential outliers or correlated errors.

The leader is a small median pool of 5 models, suggesting that selective combinations are better for this trend-dominated series. I will test a weighted combination of that same pool using inverse error to see if optimizing the weights improves the score.
Testing if a full-pool inverse-error weighting can outperform the selective small-pool strategy in a trend-dominated series.
Testing if a simple mean over the full pool provides a more stable baseline than the current leader's selective weighted approach, given the moderate ranking stability.

The trend_dominated regime and the combination_hint for selective combinations suggest that small, high-performing pools are better than the full pool. Since the current leader uses a weighted approach on pool6, I will test the median on the same pool to see if a robust central tendency performs better than inverse-error weighting.

The trend-dominated regime and moderate ranking tau suggest that a selective approach with top performers is effective, as seen in the leader. I will now test if a trimmed mean on the small, high-performing pool (pool1) can mitigate the impact of outliers or misaligned models within that subset.

The trend-dominated nature and moderate ranking stability suggest that a simple mean over all models might be too noisy, but a more robust combination like DBA (Dynamic Baseline Averaging) on the full pool could capture the underlying structural trend more effectively.

The trend-dominated regime and moderate ranking stability suggest that a selective combination is preferred, but the current leader uses a specific weight (w4) on pool6. I will test a softmax-weighted combination on the same small subset (pool1) to see if emphasizing the highest-performing models more aggressively improves the score.
Testing if inverse error weighting on the small, high-performing pool1 can improve upon the leader.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool6 weighted by w4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.7808. Series context: trend strength 0.9427 and seasonal strength 0.1852; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.571); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.919.
